question: Ryosuke is picking up his friend from work. The odometer reads 74,568 when he picks his friend up, and it reads 74,592 when he drops his friend off at his house. Ryosuke's car gets 28 miles per gallon and the price of one gallon of gas is $\$4.05$. What was the cost of the gas that was used for Ryosuke to drive his friend back home from work? (Express your answer in dollars and round to the nearest cent.)

answer:
Ryosuke drove his friend from work to home, and the odometer readings were 74,568 when he picked up his friend and 74,592 when he dropped him off. The total miles driven is calculated as follows:

\[
74,592 - 74,568 = 24 \text{ miles}
\]

Ryosuke's car gets 28 miles per gallon. The amount of gasoline used for the trip is:

\[
\frac{24 \text{ miles}}{28 \text{ miles per gallon}} = \frac{6}{7} \text{ gallons} \approx 0.8571 \text{ gallons}
\]

The price of one gallon of gas is $4.05. The cost of the gasoline used is:

\[
0.8571 \text{ gallons} \times 4.05 \text{ dollars per gallon} = 3.471255 \text{ dollars}
\]

Rounding 3.471255 to the nearest cent gives:

\[
3.47 \text{ dollars}
\]

Thus, the cost of the gas that was used for Ryosuke to drive his friend back home from work is \(\boxed{3.47}\).
